page.title: Chime Radar — distance-gated alerts, visit paths, early camera wake

sections.heading: Alert only inside 15 feet
text: Two walk-bys, one alert — the threshold is enforced on-device, so the radio never wakes for the sidewalk.
bullets: Scout RD acquires a track at 24 ft and, because that is outside the configured 15 ft alert line, keeps it entirely local — no interrupt, no radio.
Scout RD keeps updating the track as the passer-by follows the sidewalk arc at 20–24 ft; Sentry LP and Vision HP stay asleep.
The track leaves the field and Scout RD drops it — a non-alert that cost microwatts instead of a push notification.
A second visitor turns up the walkway; Scout RD sees range fall through 15 ft and raises `RADAR_INT` to Sentry LP with range and bearing latched in its status registers.
Sentry LP wakes its radio and publishes `evt/door/motion` to Relay with trigger `radar`, `range_ft` 14.6, and the threshold in force.
Relay delivers the event to Pulse, which dedups on eventId and opens the alert.
Pulse asks Herald to notify the household.
Herald pushes "Visitor 14 ft from the door, approaching" to the resident's phone.

sections.heading: The visit path rides with the alert
text: The radar was already recording the approach before the alert existed — the 30 s ring buffer is a pre-roll for trajectories, not pixels.
bullets: From first acquisition Scout RD appends every track fix (ms offset, range, bearing) to its 30-second ring buffer, overwriting the oldest frames.
When the alert fires (Flow 1 step 4), Scout RD freezes the pre-trigger fixes as protected so the approach cannot be overwritten while the visit continues.
Sentry LP reads the full track — protected pre-roll plus live fixes — from Scout RD over SPI.
Sentry LP publishes the batch to Relay on `evt/door/track`, tagged with the same eventId as the motion event.
Relay delivers the batch to Pathworks.
Pathworks projects the fixes into yard coordinates using the stored mount calibration and assembles the aerial visit path.
Pathworks stores the path record in Vault under the eventId, beside where the clip will land.
Pathworks tells Pulse the path is ready, and Pulse has Herald update the pending notification with the path thumbnail.
The resident opens the alert and scrubs the walk-up; the app fetches path frames from Vault over HTTPS.

sections.heading: Radar wakes the camera early
text: Trajectory buys the camera a 4-second head start — the waterfall shows RECORD landing while the visitor is still 9 ft out.
bullets: Scout RD tracks an approach crossing the 15 ft line inbound at 3.1 ft/s and raises `RADAR_INT` to Sentry LP with range and closing speed.
Sentry LP computes time-to-door (~4 s) and raises `WAKE_INT` to Vision HP before touching the radio — the camera gets the head start.
Vision HP powers its sensor rail and boots the encoder while the visitor is still ~12 ft out.
In parallel, Sentry LP publishes `evt/door/motion` to Relay.
Relay delivers the event to Pulse, and Pulse pushes the alert through Herald to the phone.
Vision HP reaches RECORD about 1.2 s after the radar trip, with the visitor still ~9 ft away — the clip opens on the approach, not on a doorbell press.
Vision HP records the visit and uploads the clip to Vault under the shared eventId.
Vault tells Pulse the clip is indexed; the event timeline now holds alert, aerial path, and clip.

bullets.text: **Vision HP thermal shutdown** — unchanged from the Chime thermal HLD: gating and alerts continue while the camera cools; clips are the only loss.

sections.heading: Tuning out the sidewalk
text: Dismissals are data — Sift reads visit paths, proposes a tighter arc, and the change rides the platform's [shadow/command path](https://github.com/doorbuzz-cloud/platform/blob/main/docs/cumulus-hld.md#L1) down to a chip register.
bullets: Herald delivers three alerts within an hour, each a sidewalk pass that grazed 14–15 ft without ever turning in.
The resident dismisses each alert; the app POSTs the dismissals to Nimbus API with the bearer token.
Nimbus verifies the token with Sentinel Auth, then forwards each dismissal to Pulse, where it is recorded against the eventId.
Pulse forwards the device's dismissal tally to Sift.
Sift joins the dismissed events with their Pathworks records and finds every dismissed track stayed outside 12 ft — the sidewalk clips the alert circle.
Sift files a suggestion with Pulse ("tighten the alert line to 11 ft"), and Herald pushes it to the resident.
The resident accepts; the app POSTs the config change to Nimbus, which, after another Sentinel check, hands it to Dispatch.
Dispatch writes the new desired state to Registry as a versioned shadow write, then publishes `cmd/door/radar-config` to Relay at QoS 1.
Relay parks the command in the doorbell's persistent session and delivers it on Sentry LP's next wake window.
Sentry LP writes the new threshold into Scout RD's config registers and acknowledges on `ack/door` with the applied shadow version — the same sidewalk pass now ends as Flow 1 step 3, silently.

bullets.text: **Pathworks / Registry / Dispatch down** — threshold changes fail as retryable API errors while the device enforces its last-applied config, so gating never stops.

sections.heading: Wifi drops — gating continues, alerts arrive late
text: **Wifi drops** — Scout RD keeps gating; Sentry LP queues events in flash and Relay's persistent session replays QoS 1 on reconnect. Alerts arrive late, but the visit path still assembles.

steps.text: Wifi drops — Sentry LP's uplink goes down
Scout RD keeps gating locally and still raises RADAR_INT on a trip — the outage never reaches the radar
Sentry LP can't publish — it queues the event in flash instead
Wifi returns
Sentry LP publishes the queued event — Relay's persistent session carries it through at QoS 1
Relay delivers to Pulse — the alert arrives late, but the visit path still assembles

sections.heading: Battery low / radar fault — duty-cycle stretch, then PIR fallback
text: **Battery low / radar fault** — below 20% Scout RD stretches its idle duty cycle (10 Hz → 2 Hz, ~0.5 s slower acquisition); below 8% the radar rail latches off and the doorbell degrades to PIR-triggered Chime (`trigger:"pir"`, `radar_fault` published).
bullets: Or after repeated Scout RD watchdog resets — the same outcome (radar rail latched off), independent of battery level.

steps.text: Normal operation — 10 Hz idle / 20 Hz tracking duty cycle
